question.problem: For the function $f(x,y)=\frac{3xy-1}{2x-3y},$ evaluate $\frac{∂f}{∂y}$ at the point $(0,-1).$
question.worked_solution:
We differentiate the given function with respect to $y,$ treating all other variables as constants. 

First, we use the quotient rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂y}(\frac{3xy-1}{2x-3y}) & =\frac{\frac{∂}{∂y}(3xy-1)\cdot (2x-3y)-(3xy-1)\cdot \frac{∂}{∂y}(2x-3y)}{(2x-3y)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{3x\cdot (2x-3y)-(3xy-1)\cdot (-3)}{(2x-3y)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{6{x}^{2}-9xy+9xy-3}{(2x-3y)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{6{x}^{2}-3}{(2x-3y)^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Finally, we evaluate the partial derivative at the point $(0,-1):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x}{|}_{(0,-1)} & =\frac{6(0)^{2}-3}{(2(0)-3(-1))^{2}} \\  & =\frac{-3}{{3}^{2}} \\  & =-\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}
$$
